question: What is the primary purpose of performing an eye irrigation procedure?

options.A: Treating bacterial conjunctivitis with topical antibiotics
options.B: Mechanical removal of chemical splashes or foreign bodies
options.C: Lowering intraocular pressure in glaucoma patients
options.D: Dilating the pupil for a comprehensive retinal exam

explanation: Irrigation acts primarily to flush out hazardous substances and debris physically from the ocular surface to prevent chemical burns or abrasions. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why is immediate eye irrigation critical following an alkali chemical splash?

options.A: Prompt flushing immediately restores normal intraocular pressure
options.B: Alkali substances penetrate tissues rapidly and cause deep cellular damage
options.C: Acids and alkalis neutralize each other upon contact with sterile water
options.D: Delaying irrigation increases the risk of systemic blood toxicity

explanation: Alkalis liquefy cell membranes and penetrate ocular tissues very quickly, making immediate and prolonged washing essential to halt destruction. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which condition represents an absolute contraindication for eye irrigation?

options.B: Penetrating globe injury of the eye
options.D: Superficial dust particle in the lower fornix

explanation: Fluid pressure from irrigation will worsen an open wound and expel internal eye structures, so penetrating injuries must never be flushed. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h2)

question: What makes acid and alkali chemical exposures primary indications for emergency eye irrigation?

options.A: Foreign bodies bind tightly to the lens within minutes of exposure
options.B: Chemicals immediately raise intraocular pressure to dangerous levels
options.C: Solvents cause the pupil to dilate permanently if left untreated
options.D: Corrosive agents burn and damage the surface epithelium instantly

explanation: Chemical splashes are true ocular emergencies because corrosive substances destroy surface tissues on contact and require immediate dilution. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h2)

question: Which intravenous solution is most commonly selected for standard eye irrigation?
explanation: Normal saline is isotonic, matching the natural osmolarity of tears and preventing cellular damage or swelling during prolonged flushing. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h3)

question: Why must irrigation solutions ideally be kept at room temperature rather than cold?

options.A: Cold solutions instantly crystallize upon contact with corneal proteins
options.B: Extreme temperatures trigger painful oculocardiac reflexes or vertigo
options.C: Warmed fluids dissolve chemical bonds faster than cold fluids
options.D: Chilled liquids cause the lacrimal gland to stop producing tears

explanation: Very cold or hot fluids cause severe discomfort, vertigo, and can stimulate unwanted cranial nerve reflexes in the eye. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h3)

question: How should a patient's head be positioned during an eye irrigation procedure?

options.A: Turned toward the unaffected side to protect the healthy eye
options.B: Held upright and completely stationary without any movement
options.C: Tilted backward completely to open the upper conjunctival sac
options.D: Tilted slightly toward the affected side to direct runoff away

explanation: Tilting the head toward the bad eye prevents contaminated drainage from flowing across the bridge of the nose into the healthy eye. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h4)

question: What is the clinical rationale for performing a baseline visual acuity test prior to irrigation?

options.A: It relaxes the orbicularis oculi muscle to ease eyelid opening
options.B: It determines the exact pH level of the anterior chamber fluid
options.C: It documents visual function status before potential treatment changes occur
options.D: It proves whether an open globe injury is present or absent

explanation: Establishing baseline visual acuity helps track injury severity and legal documentation before any interventions take place. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h4)

question: In which direction should the stream of irrigation fluid flow across the eye?

options.A: Directly downward from the center of the cornea
options.B: From the outer canthus toward the inner canthus
options.C: From the inner canthus toward the outer canthus
options.D: Upward from the lower fornix toward the brow

explanation: Irrigating from the inner corner to the outer corner prevents washing debris or chemicals down into the nasolacrimal duct system. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why is a topical ophthalmic anesthetic frequently administered before a chemical eye flush?

options.A: It prevents the lacrimal gland from producing irritating tears
options.B: It relieves intense muscle spasms of the eyelids that block access
options.C: It neutralizes alkaline chemical compounds on the corneal surface
options.D: It dilates the pupil so irrigation fluid reaches the posterior chamber

explanation: Chemical burns cause severe pain and involuntary eyelid squeezing (blepharospasm), which topical anesthetics relieve to allow proper flushing. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h5)

question: What is the normal physiological pH range of the ocular tear film to verify after chemical irrigation?
explanation: A neutral pH between 7.0 and 7.3 indicates that chemical residues have been fully diluted and washed away from the eye. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is an essential documentation requirement following an emergency eye irrigation procedure?

options.A: The patient's family medical history regarding eye disease
options.B: Total volume of fluid used and the duration of irrigation
options.C: The exact brand name of the emesis basin utilized
options.D: The number of sterile drapes discarded in the bin

explanation: Recording exact fluid volume and duration is critical for clinical continuity, especially when monitoring severe chemical injury recovery. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h6)

question: Which complication can occur if the irrigation nozzle or tubing touches the eye surface during the flush?
explanation: Direct mechanical contact between equipment and the delicate cornea causes surface scratches and abrasions. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is the immediate nursing action if a patient develops severe worsening eye pain and decreased vision midway through an irrigation procedure?

options.A: Increase the flow rate to flush out any remaining debris faster
options.B: Apply an eye patch tightly while continuing the fluid flow
options.C: Switch from normal saline to sterile water for better cooling
options.D: Stop the irrigation immediately and notify the physician

explanation: Worsening pain or vision loss indicates potential complications such as corneal damage or increased pressure, requiring an immediate provider evaluation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h7)
